messages:
Maya: quick Q — trying to make a subchart use an existing kubernetes secret if provided, otherwise create one with a deterministic name. doing this at chart level so apps can opt-in to external secrets. examples?
Jon: you can guard with an if on .Values.myapp.externalSecretName and fall back to a generated name. are you using umbrella chart overrides or subchart values? :eyes:
Maya: umbrella chart. subchart has templates/secret.yaml that should not error if externalSecretName is set to empty string. also want to use .Release.Name in the generated name.
Liam: simplest pattern i use:

```
{{- $ext := .Values.externalSecretName }}
{{- if $ext }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: {{ $ext }}
  annotations:
    external: "true"
data: {}
{{- else }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: {{ printf "%s-%s" .Release.Name .Chart.Name | trunc 63 | trimSuffix "-" }}
data:
  ...
{{- end }}
```

Liam: note: if umbrella sets `mychart.externalSecretName: null` helm treats null vs empty differently — prefer explicit empty string or absent key.
Olivia: watch out for subchart value scoping: umbrella should set `subchartName.externalSecretName:` not `externalSecretName` at root unless you use global. if you want a global override use `.Values.global.externalSecrets.myapp`.
Carla: if you want to reference an external k8s secret (not create), don't emit a Secret resource at all. have your deployment envFrom reference the provided name:

```
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ default (printf "%s-%s" .Release.Name .Chart.Name) .Values.externalSecretName }}
```

Carla: that way, when externalSecretName is set helm substitutes it, otherwise it uses the generated name the chart created.
Maya: nice — does `default` work when the umbrella has `externalSecretName: null`? i've seen it still pick null and output an empty string.
Jon: default treats empty string as a value. null is considered missing, default will fill when the value is absent or null. but if umbrella sets `externalSecretName: ""` then default won't replace. so prefer not setting empty string in umbrella.
sre-bot: helm lint: warning: templates/secret.yaml: secret name exceeds 63 chars, truncated — might break lookups if you expect exact name.
Liam: also be careful with `trunc` behaviour, it might cut important suffix. consider hashing part of the name if you need uniqueness and length safety.
Olivia: last tip — for optional external secret pattern, add a values helper so it's consistent:

```
{{- define "mychart.secretName" -}}
{{- default (printf "%s-%s" .Release.Name .Chart.Name) .Values.externalSecretName -}}
{{- end -}}
```

and reuse `{{ include "mychart.secretName" . }}` in templates.
Maya: awesome, thanks. i'll switch umbrella to set absent/null or a concrete name, add the helper, and avoid emitting a resource when external is set. will ping if helm template still complains.
Jon: green :thumbsup:
Carla: :lock: also check your RBAC for whoever creates the secret in CI if you go that route.
Maya: noted, thanks everyone!
